Universe expected to decay in 10⁷⁸ years, much sooner than previously thought
by
Netherlands Research School for Astronomy
Artistic impression of a neutron star that is 'evaporating' slowly via Hawking-like radiation. Credit: Daniëlle Futselaar/artsource.nl
The universe is decaying much faster than thought. This is shown by calculations of three Dutch scientists on the so-called Hawking radiation. They calculate that the last stellar remnants take about 10
78
years to perish. That is much shorter than the previously postulated 10
1100
years.
The researchers have published their findings in the
Journal of Cosmology and Astroparticle Physics
.
The research by black hole expert Heino Falcke, quantum physicist Michael Wondrak, and mathematician Walter van Suijlekom (all from Radboud University, Nijmegen, the Netherlands) is a follow-up to a
2023 paper by the same trio
.
In that paper, they showed that not only
black holes
, but also other objects such as
neutron stars
, can "evaporate" via a process akin to Hawking
radiation
. After that publication, the researchers received many questions from inside and outside the scientific community about how long the process would take. They have now answered this question in the new article.
Ultimate end
The researchers calculated that the end of the universe is about 10
78
years away, if only Hawking-like radiation is taken into account. This is the time it takes for white dwarf stars, the most persistent celestial bodies, to decay via Hawking-like radiation.
Previous studies, which did not take this effect into account, put the lifetime of white dwarfs at 10
1100
years. Lead author Heino Falcke said, "So the ultimate end of the universe comes much sooner than expected, but fortunately it still takes a very long time."
The researchers did the calculations dead-seriously and with a wink. The basis is a reinterpretation of Hawking radiation. In 1975, physicist Stephen Hawking postulated that contrary to the theory of relativity, particles and radiation could escape from a black hole. At the edge of a black hole, two temporary particles can form, and before they merge, one particle is sucked into the black hole and the other particle escapes.
One of the consequences of this so-called Hawking radiation is that a black hole very slowly decays into particles and radiation. This contradicts Albert Einstein's
theory of relativity
, which says that black holes can only grow.
Researchers calculated from ten different objects how long the 'evaporation' via Hawking-like radiation takes in an ideal environment without other influences. White dwarf stars dissolve in about 10
78
years. The human body, if only Hawking-like radiation is involved, decays in 10
90
years. Credit: Falcke, Wondrak & Van Suijlekom
Neutron star as slow as black hole
The researchers calculated that the process of Hawking radiation theoretically also applies to other objects with a
gravitational field
. The calculations further showed that the evaporation time of an object depends only on its density.
To the researchers' surprise, neutron stars and stellar black holes take the same amount of time to decay: 10
67
years. This was unexpected because black holes have a stronger gravitational field, which should cause them to evaporate faster.
"But black holes have no surface," says co-author and postdoctoral researcher Michael Wondrak, "They reabsorb some of their own radiation which inhibits the process."
Man and moon: 10
90
years
Because the researchers were at it anyway, they also calculated how long it takes for the moon and a human to evaporate via Hawking-like radiation. That's 10
90
years. Of course, the researchers subtly note, there are other processes that may cause humans and the moon to disappear faster than calculated.
Co-author Walter van Suijlekom, professor of mathematics at Radboud University, adds that the research is an exciting collaboration of different disciplines and that combining astrophysics,
quantum physics
and mathematics leads to new insights.
"By asking these kinds of questions and looking at extreme cases, we want to better understand the theory, and perhaps one day, we will unravel the mystery of Hawking radiation."
More information:
H. Falcke et al, An upper limit to the lifetime of stellar remnants from gravitational pair production,
Journal of Cosmology and Astroparticle Physics
. On
arXiv
(2024).

data.title: Stop Solving Problems by Adding Processes
data.author: acmerfight
data.article_summary: 文章主张不应通过增加审批流程来解决操作风险问题。许多团队依赖额外的审批层次，如数据库变更或服务部署需领导批准，但这些流程常沦为形式化官僚主义，无法有效提升风险控制质量。领导由于不掌握具体技术细节，难以做出合理判断。文章建议，更好的风险管控应依赖明确的风险评估标准、自动化验证工具和主动报警系统，而非增加无谓的审批流程。这些措施能更有效地应对风险，避免不必要的延迟和工作绕行。

主要讨论点：运营风险管理中的审批流程

不同观点：
• 观点一：许多SRE和运维团队通过增加额外的审批流程来管理运营风险，比如数据库 schema 更改、服务部署、客户端发布等。这种方法强调通过多层次的审核和批准来减少操作失误和潜在风险。支持者认为，这种流程可以有效防止因人为错误导致的系统故障或服务中断。
  - 论据和例子：通过审批流程，团队可以确保所有变更都经过充分的评估和验证，减少意外问题的发生。

• 观点二：过度依赖审批流程可能会导致效率低下和创新受限。批评者认为，过多的审批步骤会增加工作负担，延缓项目进度，特别是在快速迭代和敏捷开发环境中，这种做法可能不适用。
  - 论据和例子：在需要快速响应和频繁变更的环境中，过多的审批流程可能成为瓶颈，导致团队无法及时应对市场需求和技术变化。

• 观点三：有些评论者提出可以采用自动化工具和监控系统来替代部分人工审批流程。他们认为，通过自动化可以实现风险管理与效率之间的平衡，既能减少人为错误，又能提高响应速度。
  - 论据和例子：自动化工具可以实时监控系统状态，自动检测潜在风险并进行必要的调整，而不需要人为干预。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于如何在风险管理和效率之间找到平衡。一些团队倾向于严格的审批流程以确保系统稳定性，而另一些团队则希望通过自动化和简化流程来提高效率和响应速度。
• 不同团队和项目可能需要根据实际情况调整策略，找到最适合他们的风险管理方法。
• 还有评论提到，团队文化和经验也会影响对审批流程的依赖程度，经验丰富的团队可能更少依赖额外的审批步骤。

Stop Solving Problems by Adding Processes
Many SRE and operations teams predominantly address operational risks through “additional approval processes” — whether for database schema changes, service deployments, client releases, etc.
In theory, such operations should be planned, scheduled, and reviewed by the designated project owner. However, organizations often impose redundant layers requiring approvals from the owner’s direct leader, or even higher-level leadership. The justification typically cites leadership’s “accountability,” implying they consequently deserve oversight rights.
Yet practitioners understand this approval mechanism often degenerates into performative bureaucracy. Leaders cannot reasonably comprehend technical specifics across multiple projects — if a leader truly masters a project’s details, they should inherently
be
the project owner.
Key arguments:
Increased process cost ≠ Improved risk control quality
Using approval layers as risk “gates” constitutes an indirect and inefficient control mechanism. It indiscriminately delays critical emergency changes and incentivizes workarounds, while failing to enhance substantive risk assessment capabilities.
Effective risk mitigation requires:
Clear risk evaluation criteria and tooling for owners
Enhanced automated validation and proactive alerting systems
Mandatory justification protocols for high-risk operations during critical periods
These fundamental measures prove more impactful than adding perfunctory approval layers that often succumb to information asymmetry or leadership bandwidth constraints.

U.S. and China agree to slash tariffs for 90 days in major trade breakthrough
Squawk Box
The U.S. and China on Monday agreed to temporarily suspend most tariffs on each other's goods in a move that shows a major thawing of trade tensions between the world's two largest economies.
The trade agreement means that "reciprocal" tariffs between both countries will be cut from 125% to 10%. The U.S.'
20% duties on Chinese imports relating to fentanyl
will remain in place, meaning total tariffs on China stand at 30%.
The breakthrough comes after U.S. and China trade representatives held high-stakes talks in Switzerland over the weekend.
"We had very productive talks and I believe that the venue, here in Lake Geneva, added great equanimity to what was a very positive process," U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in a news conference.
"We have reached an agreement on a 90-day pause and substantially move down the tariff levels. Both sides on the reciprocal tariffs will move their tariffs down 115%," Bessent said.
The pause will begin Wednesday. Both China and the U.S. said they will continue discussions on economic and trade policy.
Stocks jump on news of deal
Since returning to the White House in January, U.S. President
Donald Trump
has launched a flurry of aggressive trade measures that
jolted financial markets
and
ratcheted up recession fears
. The duties, which are designed to
narrow the U.S. trade deficit
, hit China particularly hard.
Trump had imposed tariffs of up to 145% on Chinese imports, prompting Beijing to respond with retaliatory curbs of its own, including restrictions on some rare earth elements.
Investors were buoyed by news of the tariff reprieve. Stateside,
Nasdaq futures
pointed to a 3.7% gain, with
S&P 500
futures higher by 2.7% and the
Dow
up by more than 840 points, or 2%.

Why Pope Leo chose his name: AI, workers' rights, new Industrial Revolution
India and Pakistan agree to immediate ceasefire
Newark mayor arrested for alleged trespass at New Jersey ICE detention facility
The
ICE U.S. Dollar Index
also rose sharply. The index, which measures the U.S. dollar against a basket of global currencies, was last up 1.1% to 101.46.
Elsewhere, the pan-European
Stoxx 600
index
climbed by around 1%
during midmorning deals.
Oil prices also popped. International benchmark
Brent
crude futures with July expiry traded more than 2.7% higher at $65.66 a barrel, while U.S.
West Texas Intermediate
futures stood at $62.81, up 2.9% for the session.
'Keeps the pressure on'
Mark Williams, chief Asia economist at Capital Economics, described the trade war truce as "a substantial de-escalation."
"However, the US still has much higher tariffs on China than on other countries and still appears to be trying to rally other countries to introduce restrictions of their own on trade with China," Williams said in a research note.
"In these circumstances, there is no guarantee that the 90-day truce will give way to a lasting ceasefire," he added.
Meanwhile, Tai Hui, APAC chief market strategist at J.P. Morgan Asset Management, said the magnitude of the U.S.-China tariff reduction was larger than expected.
"This reflects both sides recognizing the economic reality that tariffs will hit global growth and negotiation is a better option going forward," Hui said in a research note.
"The 90-day period may not be sufficient for the two sides to reach a detailed agreement, but it keeps the pressure on the negotiation process," he added.
Hui noted that investors were still waiting for further details on other trade terms, such as whether China would relax rare earth export restrictions.
— CNBC's Ganesh Rao contributed to this report.

data.title: Eagle Hunters of Kyrgyzstan
data.author: gmays
data.article_summary: 文章讲述了吉尔吉斯斯坦的鹰猎人如何努力保持一种古老的传统。主人翁Talgar Shaybyrov与他的金雕Tumara共同生活和狩猎了二十年后，按照习俗将雕放归自然。鹰猎人（burkutchu）通过世代相传保持这一传统，训练雕需要数月时间，猎人与雕之间的关系非常密切。虽然鹰猎曾是游牧生活中重要的生存技能，但现在一些人如Talgar的侄子Nursultan Kolbaev通过为游客表演鹰猎来赚取收入，并曾在2014年世界游牧运动会上获得冠军。然而，这种转变也引发了对传统与商业化之间平衡的讨论。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：有关鹰猎活动（eagle hunting）的背景、地域分布、文化意义以及相关争议。

不同观点：
• **ENadyr**：认为鹰猎并非吉尔吉斯斯坦独有，而是在哈萨克斯坦、蒙古等地也广泛存在。他提到纪录片《女猎鹰者》（The Eagle Huntress, 2016）展示了蒙古一位女性进入这一传统上由男性主导的领域。

• **stevage**：基于自己在吉尔吉斯斯坦的旅行经历，提到鹰猎者通过让游客与鹰拍照获取小费，并描述了当地人对鹰猎的热情。他还分享了对该国整体的积极印象，特别是徒步旅行的机会。

• **zabil**：强调鹰猎主要是一种哈萨克族的传统，而不是吉尔吉斯斯坦特有的。他提到自己在蒙古Ölgii参加鹰猎节时，看到一名少女赢得比赛，并指出由于旅游业的发展，这一传统重新焕发了活力。

• **marvstazar**：提供了一个音乐视频链接（Ummet Ozcan的"Kayra"），展示了鹰猎者的画面，补充了视觉材料。

• **adamkaz42**：提供了《女猎鹰者》电影的链接，补充了有关该纪录片的参考资料。

• **lukan**：对鹰猎的具体狩猎方式和鹰的作用感到困惑，认为没有详细说明鹰如何帮助猎人捕猎。同时，还提到文字排版问题影响阅读体验。

• **anovikov**：认为按现代标准，鹰的训练方式可能涉及动物虐待，提出对该传统的伦理质疑。

• **Hobadee**：与lukan有相似误解，最初以为鹰猎是猎杀鹰，而不是用鹰来打猎。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是鹰猎活动是否涉及动物虐待，特别是现代社会对动物权益的关注使得鹰猎的训练方式受到质疑。
• 不同用户提供了额外的多媒体资料（如纪录片和音乐视频），丰富了讨论内容。
• 对鹰猎文化的误解（如误以为猎杀鹰）也成为讨论的一部分，显示出对该传统缺乏了解。

43911152.article_content:
Like what you’re reading?
Subscribe to
The Atavist Magazine
today for access to our full archive.
The
Eagle
Hunters
of
Kyrgyzstan
In the mountains of Central Asia, a Small group of outdoorsmen are keeping an ancient tradition alive.
Photographs by
yam g-Jun
Published April 2025
In the spring of 2021, Talgar Shaybyrov embarked on a heartbreaking journey. For twenty years, Talgar had hunted with a golden eagle he called Tumara. The two lived at nearly 6,000 feet above sea level, in the quiet town of Bokonbaevo, Kyrgyzstan, where guesthouses and yurt camps line the shore of Issyk Kul, the world’s second-largest saltwater lake. They had spent the past two decades hunting jackals and foxes together, often traveling in Talgar’s run-down Volkswagen Golf, a modern replacement for a horse. Now Talgar was ready to return Tumara to the wilderness, as was the custom among eagle hunters. Doing so allows the birds a chance to mate and be free as they near the end of their long lives. “I have spent so many years with her,” Talgar told me. “I hope she will enjoy her freedom.”
Kyrgyzstan’s eagle hunters, or
burkutchu,
carry on a long-standing tradition. For centuries, hunting with an eagle was essential to the region’s nomadic lifestyle: A good hunter could help feed and clothe a village. One family member typically teaches another, and it begins when a hunter finds a nest with multiple eaglets and chooses one to raise. It can take three months to train and raise a fledgling. The hunters spend years with their birds, and the relationship can take on an almost human quality. “Suluuke is like a daughter to me,” said Nursultan Kolbaev, Talgar’s nephew, of the bird he began training in 2012.
While
burkutchu
still use the eagles to hunt, many like Nursaltan also view the endeavor as a sport—and a way to make a living. Nursaltan was named eagle-hunting champion at the 2014 World Nomad Games. As travel to the region flourished, he turned to performing for tourists. This provides income for Nursultan’s family, but he’s been criticized for sacrificing tradition for profit. As Talgar began training his next eagle, the
burkutchu
community grappled with a changing world and what it might mean for the centuries-old relationship between humans and the eagles they train.
Talgar Shaybyrov leads a hunt in Bokonbaevo, October 2020. Hunters often work in groups—on horseback and traveling by car—to increase the chance of a successful hunt.
Bokonbaevo, with Issyk Kul and the Tian Shan range in the distance.
Right and below: Nursultan and Suluuke in Fairytale Canyon. During training, each success is rewarded with a piece of meat.
Left: Nursultan with Suluuke and his son at their home. The white hat Nursultan wears is called an
ak-kalpak;
the leather hood on Suluuke is called a
tomogo
. Below: Nursultan shows off a medal from the World Nomad Games; he’s a former champion in eagle hunting.
Right and below: Nursultan on a hunt in Jalal-Abad in December 2021 with Suluuke and his dog.
The Taigan is a breed of sight hound native to Kyrgyzstan. They are used to flush prey, such as foxes, on a hunt.
Right and below: In December 2021, eagle hunters in Bokonbaevo invited those from other parts of Kyrgyzstan for a joint expedition. The night before, 20 eagle hunters attended a
sherine
, or gathering. The event allowed them to connect with
burkutchu
from around the country—and size up the competition for the World Nomad Games.
Nursultan and Suluuke give an eagle-hunting demonstration for tourists. On a good day, he can earn $500 for ten demonstrations.
Most Kyrgyz farm on a small scale to help feed their families. Nursultan’s family rent about four acres of land to grow wheat.
Right and below: The Kyrgyz National Day Games, a national competition, in August 2022.
Left and below: Nursultan and Suluuke competing at the Kyrgyz National Day Games.

data.title: Vision Now Available in Llama.cpp
data.author: redman25
data.article_summary: **llama.cpp** 是由 **ggml-org** 开发的一个开源项目，旨在通过C语言实现对Facebook的LLaMA（大型语言模型）的高效运行和推理。该项目特别关注在本地和低资源环境下（如个人电脑、嵌入式设备）运行大语言模型，而不依赖于大规模的云计算资源。项目使用了GGML（Generic Graph Machine Learning）库，专注于优化性能和内存使用。截至目前，该项目在GitHub上获得了79.8k个星标，显示了其在社区中的广泛关注和使用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对llama.cpp及其多模态模型（特别是Gemma系列）的性能、使用方法、以及在不同硬件上的运行情况展开的讨论。

data.title: University of Texas-led team solves a big problem for fusion energy
data.author: signa11
data.article_summary: 研究团队解决了核聚变能量领域一个长期存在的问题，使得设计无泄漏的磁约束系统速度提高了10倍，且不牺牲准确性。核聚变反应堆的一个主要挑战是高能粒子泄漏，这阻碍了等离子体的足够高温和高密度以维持核聚变反应。传统方法依赖牛顿运动定律，计算时间极长，而简化的扰动理论又不准确。新方法利用对称性理论，有效解决了自1950年代以来悬而未决的难题，尤其适用于一种名为仿星器的核聚变反应堆设计，并可应用于托卡马克设计中的电子泄漏问题。这一突破加速了清洁能源的实现。

主要讨论点：关于核融合研究及其可行性的多角度讨论

不同观点：
• [munchler] 认为，受能源部资助的研究项目中，类似“数据驱动”和“非微扰”的表述将变得越来越少见，暗示对未来资助的担忧。
• [scythe] 对论文中的“数据驱动”和“非微扰”结合表示惊讶，但通过解释论文中的方法，表明该研究并非只是依赖机器学习的“黑箱”操作，而是有正式数学解法，并通过数据填补未知参数。他通过类比简单物理问题（如抛物运动）帮助理解该研究的核心思想。
• [jmyeet] 对核融合作为商业可行能源持怀疑态度，认为工程挑战巨大且成本高昂，即便技术上可行，资本投入和中子损失等问题可能使其不具经济性。他还对比了核融合与太阳能，认为太阳能更有未来。

43962148.article_content:
AUSTIN, Texas —  Abundant, low-cost, clean energy — the envisioned result if scientists and engineers can successfully produce a reliable method of generating and sustaining fusion energy — took one step closer to reality, as a team of researchers from The University of Texas at Austin, Los Alamos National Laboratory and Type One Energy Group solved a longstanding problem in the field.
One of the big challenges holding fusion energy back has been the ability to contain high-energy particles inside fusion reactors. When high-energy alpha particles leak from a reactor, that prevents the plasma from getting hot and dense enough to sustain the fusion reaction. To prevent them from leaking, engineers design elaborate magnetic confinement systems, but there are often holes in the magnetic field, and a tremendous amount of computational time is required to predict their locations and eliminate them.
In their paper published in
Physical Review Letters
, the research team describes having discovered a shortcut that can help engineers design leak-proof magnetic confinement systems 10 times as fast as the gold standard method, without sacrificing accuracy. While several other big challenges remain for all magnetic fusion designs, this advance addresses the biggest challenge that’s specific to a type of fusion reactor first proposed in the 1950s, called a stellarator.
“What’s most exciting is that we’re solving something that’s been an open problem for almost 70 years,” said Josh Burby, assistant professor of physics at UT and first author of the paper. “It’s a paradigm shift in how we design these reactors.”
A stellarator uses external coils carrying electric currents that generate magnetic fields to confine a plasma and high-energy particles. This confinement system is often described as a “magnetic bottle.”
There is a way to identify where the holes are in the magnetic bottle using Newton’s laws of motion, which is very precise but takes an enormous amount of computational time. Worse still, to design a stellarator, scientists might need to simulate hundreds or thousands of slightly different designs, tweaking the layout of the magnetic coils and iterating to eliminate the holes — a process that would require a prohibitive amount of computation on top of that.
So, to save time and money, scientists and engineers routinely use a simpler method for approximating where the holes are, using an approach called perturbation theory. But that method is much less accurate, which has slowed the development of stellarators. The new method relies on symmetry theory, a different way of understanding the system.
“There is currently no practical way to find a theoretical answer to the alpha-particle confinement question without our results,” Burby said. “Direct application of Newton’s laws is too expensive. Perturbation methods commit gross errors. Ours is the first theory that circumvents these pitfalls.”
This new method also can help with a similar but different problem in another popular magnetic fusion reactor design called a tokamak. In that design, there’s a problem with runaway electrons — high-energy electrons that can punch a hole in the surrounding walls. This new method can help identify holes in the magnetic field where these electrons might leak.
Burby’s co-authors from UT are postdoctoral researcher Max Ruth and graduate student Ivan Maldonado. Other authors are Dan Messenger, a postdoctoral fellow at Los Alamos, and Leopoldo Carbajal, a computational scientist and data scientist at Type One Energy Group, a company planning to build stellarators for power generation.
This work was supported by the U.S. Department of Energy.

data.title: Ruby 3.5 Feature: Namespace on read
data.author: ksec
data.article_summary:
这篇文章介绍了Ruby中一个新的实验性功能提案，即通过“读取时命名空间”（Namespace on Read）来定义虚拟顶层命名空间。该功能允许在不同命名空间中分别加载和要求库文件，从而避免库之间的名称冲突，并支持加载同一gem的不同版本。该功能最初通过环境变量`RUBY_NAMESPACE=1`启用，默认情况下是禁用的。

文章详细说明了“写入时命名空间”（On Write）和“读取时命名空间”（On Read）两种方法的区别，并展示了如何使用`Namespace.new`创建新命名空间及其实现细节。不同命名空间中的常量、类变量、全局变量和方法相互隔离，确保独立运行。文章还提供了示例代码，展示了如何在不同命名空间中加载和使用模块及类。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Ruby新命名空间功能的价值和潜在问题

不同观点：
• 反对观点1：ezekg认为这个功能解决了一个实际中很少存在的问题，尤其是像byroot这样有丰富经验的开发者也持相同看法，建议取消该功能。gitroom和baggy_trough也表达了类似担忧，认为新功能增加了不必要的复杂性，可能带来更多问题而不是解决问题。
• 支持观点1：jacobevelyn分享了一个实际使用场景，在gem的维护中需要对比不同分支和多个gem的性能，当前需要用一些“hacky”手段，因此这个功能在特定情况下是有价值的，但也认同byroot等人的担忧。
• 技术比较观点：irjustin建议Ruby采用像Python或JavaScript那样的显式导入机制，以解决“魔法”问题和命名空间冲突。usrbinenv则对比了Go的导入机制，认为Go的默认命名空间可能更好。
• 历史与设计观点：frou_dh提到Ruby的设计受到Lisp和Emacs Lisp的启发，具有一个大而动态的命名空间，这使得Monkey Patch非常方便。benatkin将该功能与JavaScript的ShadowRealm提案进行比较。
• 实际应用与生态担忧：dudeinjapan担心新功能会被滥用，导致Ruby生态中的混乱，尤其是常量重定义的问题。JohnBooty则认为这个功能在短期内是有用的“拐杖”，但担心它会鼓励不好的编码实践。

补充讨论：
• 关于就业和语言选择的讨论：zwnow提到对Ruby的兴趣，但更关心就业前景，考虑学习Elixir/Phoenix和JavaScript框架。
• 安全与历史文章：felipemesquita分享了一篇关于npm安全性的文章，指出多版本依赖同时加载可能带来的复杂性。

争议焦点：
• 新功能的价值和必要性：一方认为新功能解决了实际问题，另一方认为它增加了不必要的复杂性，并可能破坏现有生态。
• 对Ruby生态的影响：担心新功能会导致滥用，破坏现有约定和编码习惯。

Description
This replaces
#19744
Concept
¶
This proposes a new feature to define virtual top-level namespaces in Ruby. Those namespaces can require/load libraries (either .rb or native extension) separately from other namespaces. Dependencies of required/loaded libraries are also required/loaded in the namespace.
This feature will be disabled by default at first, and will be enabled by an env variable
RUBY_NAMESPACE=1
as an experimental feature.
(It could be enabled by default in the future possibly.)
"on read" approach
¶
The "on write" approach here is the design to define namespaces on the loaded side. For example, Java packages are defined in the .java files and it is required to separate namespaces from each other. It can be implemented very easily, but it requires all libraries to be updated with the package declaration. (In my opinion, it's almost impossible in the Ruby ecosystem.)
The "on read" approach is to create namespaces and then require/load applications and libraries in them. Programmers can control namespace separation at the "read" time. So, we can introduce the namespace separation incrementally.
Motivation
¶
The "namespace on read" can solve the 2 problems below, and can make a path to solve another problem:
Avoiding name conflicts between libraries
Applications can require two different libraries safely which use the same module name.
Avoiding unexpected globally shared modules/objects
Applications can make an independent/unshared module instance.
Multiple versions of gems can be required
Application developers will have fewer version conflicts between gem dependencies if rubygems/bundler will support the namespace on read. (Support from RubyGems/Bundler and/or other packaging systems will be needed)
For the motivation details, see [Feature
#19744
].

Namespace specification
¶
Types of namespaces
¶
There are two namespace types, "root" and "user" namespace. "Root" namespace exists solely in a Ruby process, and "user" namespaces can be created as many as Ruby programmers want.
Root namespace
¶
Root namespace is a unique namespace to be defined when a Ruby process starts. It only contains built-in classes/modules/constants, which are available without any
require
calls, including RubyGems itself (when
--disable-gems
is not specified).
At here, "builtin" classes/modules are classes/modules accessible when users' script evaluation starts, without any require/load calls.
User namespace
¶
User namespace is a namespace to run users' Ruby scripts. The "main" namespace is the namespace to run the user's
.rb
script specified by the
ruby
command-line argument. Other user namespaces ("optional" namespaces) can be created by
Namespace.new
call.
In user namespace (both main and optional namespaces), built-in class/module definitions are copied from the root namespace, and other new classes/modules are defined in the namespace, separately from other (root/user) namespaces.
The newly defined classes/modules are top-level classes/modules in the main namespace like
App
, but in optional namespaces, classes/modules are defined under the namespace (subclass of Module), like
ns::App
.
In that namespace
ns
,
ns::App
is accessible as
App
(or
::App
). There is no way to access
App
in the main namespace from the code in the different namespace
ns
.
Constants, class variables and global variables
¶
Constants, Class variables of built-in classes and global variables are also separated by namespace. Values set to class/global variables in a namespace are invisible in other namespaces.
Methods and procs
¶
Methods defined in a namespace run with the defined namespace, even when called from other namespaces.
Procs created in a namespace run with the defined namespace too.

这篇文章介绍了Ruby中一个新的实验性功能提案，即通过“读取时命名空间”（Namespace on Read）来定义虚拟顶层命名空间。该功能允许在不同命名空间中分别加载和要求库文件，从而避免库之间的名称冲突，并支持加载同一gem的不同版本。该功能最初通过环境变量`RUBY_NAMESPACE=1`启用，默认情况下是禁用的。

文章详细说明了“写入时命名空间”（On Write）和“读取时命名空间”（On Read）两种方法的区别，并展示了如何使用`Namespace.new`创建新命名空间及其实现细节。不同命名空间中的常量、类变量、全局变量和方法相互隔离，确保独立运行。文章还提供了示例代码，展示了如何在不同命名空间中加载和使用模块及类。

data.title: Spade Hardware Description Language
data.author: spmcl
data.article_summary: Spade是一种新的硬件描述语言，旨在简化硬件描述并减少错误。它借鉴了软件编程语言的优点，增加了对常见硬件结构的语言级别支持，同时不影响对生成硬件的底层控制。其主要特性包括：第一类管道构造、强大的类型系统（包括结构体、数组、元组和带关联负载的枚举）、模式匹配以及类型推断。Spade的编译器提供详细的错误信息，并附带一系列工具，如构建工具Swim和测试工具cocotb。未来计划包括整数范围作为类型、带特性的泛型、时钟域信息推断等。尽管文档仍在完善中，Spade处于早期阶段，但用户可以通过相关书籍和演讲了解更多并开始使用。

主要讨论点：新硬件描述语言（HDL）的潜力和挑战

不同观点：
• Lramseyer认为新语言的开发者在开源硬件社区做了很多有价值的工作，并指出了HDL相较于常规软件语言在时间和空间编程上的独特挑战。
• smallpipe担心生成的不易读的SystemVerilog代码会影响使用，因为SV是业界标准工具的语言。

• fjfaase提到了基于Haskell的Clash语言，并提供了相关资源链接，指出Clash也是一个活跃发展的HDL选项。
• kayson提到另一个新HDL VeryL，认为新语言要取代SystemVerilog还有很长的路要走。

• chrsw认为新语言在解决数字设计表达问题的同时，保留了传统HDL的心理模型，达到了一个良好的平衡。
• raluk提出了关于如何编写循环电路的问题，并给出了一个IIR滤波器的示例原型。
• adwn欢迎将现代编程语言概念引入硬件设计的尝试，但担心新语言的开发者缺乏足够的FPGA设计经验，可能会解决错误的问题。

补充讨论：
• 新HDL的验证功能被认为是关键，特别是验证过程占据了设计工作的主要部分。
• 不同用户对新语言的学习曲线和代码可读性有不同看法，反映了在接受新工具方面的普遍挑战。
• 有争议的焦点在于新语言开发者是否具备足够的领域经验，以及新语言是否能有效解决实际设计中的痛点。
• 一些评论者对现有HDL（如Verilog和VHDL）的局限性表示不满，并期待新语言能带来变革。

Table of Contents
Spade
Key Features
Using Spade
Publications
Talks
Development
License
Spade
Spade is a new hardware description language which makes hardware
description easier and less error-prone. It does this by taking lessons from
software programming languages, and adding language level support for common
hardware constructs, all without compromising low level control over what
hardware gets generated.
Key Features
Language Level Pipelines
Pipelines are a first class construct in Spade, making re-timing and
re-pipelining trivial. The
reg
separates code into stages, meaning you never
have to manually define pipeline registers, and that behavior is separated
from physical implementation.
When you need to update your design to meet timing, you can simply add or move
reg
statements. The compiler is
smart enough to figure out when these changes affect the timing of instantiating
modules and tells you where to update your code to keep the original behavior.
pipeline
(
4
) X(clk
:
clk
,
a
:
int<32>
,
b
:
int<32>)
->
int<64> {
let
product
=
a
*
b
;
reg
*
3
;
let
result
=
f
(a
,
product)
;
reg
;
result
}
For more complex pipelines with feedback, such as a processor data path,
re-timing becomes less trivial, but being able to reason about signals in
stages instead of individual registers is still very helpful.
Types and Enums
Spade has a powerful type system with structs, arrays, tuples and
sum types
called
enums
.
A strong type system makes interoperability with external or internal modules
easier, and means you can refactor your code with confidence. The compiler will
tell you where your changes affect the behavior of your code.
Enums are of particular importance: unlike the enums of C and Verilog, they can
have associated payload.
You can model a value which may or may not be available with the
Option
enum:
enum
Option
<T> {
Some
(val
:
T)
,
None
}
Or why not model the instruction set of a CPU?
enum
Insn
{
Set { dreg
:
int<5>
,
val
:
int<32> }
,
Add { dreg
:
int<5>
,
lhs
:
int<5>
,
rhs
:
int<5> }
,
Sub { dreg
:
int<5>
,
lhs
:
int<5>
,
rhs
:
int<5> }
,
Jump { target
:
int<32> }
}
The compiler ensures that fields can only be accessed if the value is of the
correct type. For example, if the instruction is a
Jump
, there is no way to
access a
dreg
field.
Pattern Matching
Enums work really well with pattern matching which allows you to check
conditions and easily bind sub-values to variables.
You can easily build an ALU:
fn
alu
(
insn
:
Insn,
rs1
:
int<32>,
rs2
:
int<32>)
->
int<32> {
let
adder_result
=
match
insn {
Insn
::
Add(
_
,
_
,
_
)
=>
rs1
+
rs2
,
Insn
::
Sub(
_
,
_
,
_
)
=>
rs1
-
rs2
,
Insn
::
Set(
_
,
val)
=>
sext
(val)
,
Insn
::
Jump(
_
)
=>
0
,
}
;
trunc
(adder_result)
}
Or select the first of two values, and 0 if none are present:
let
result
=
match
(a
,
b) {
(
Some
(x)
,
_
)
=>
x
,
(
_
,
Some
(x))
=>
x
,
_ =>
0
}
The compiler makes sure that all cases are covered. For example, if you add a
new instruction to the
Insn
type, it will force you to deal with that case in
the ALU.
Type inference
Spade has powerful type inference which gives you the benefits of static types,
without all the typing.
Great Error Messages
The compiler should be your friend. Error messages give you as much information
as possible
error: Match branches have incompatible type
30 +-Insn::Add(_, _, _) => rs1 + rs2,
|                       ^^^^^^^^^
|                       This branch has type int<33>
32 | Insn::Set(_, val) => val,
|                      ^^^ But this one has type int<32>
|
= Expected: 33 in: int<33>
=      Got: 32 in: int<32>
Bad error messages are considered a bug. Please report them!
Helpful tooling
Spade comes with a great set of tools around the language
The official build tool
Swim
manages
your dependencies, calls synthesis tools and runs your tests. It can even
create a new project for you with a single command!
Of course you can put the generated Verilog into your regular build flow
as well.
Tests are written in
cocotb
allowing you to take
advantage of python for all your testing needs. When you need higher
performance tests, you can also use
verilator
VCDs coming out of tests are automatically translated to include Spade type
information so you never have to decode individual bits in your waveform.
Planned features
There are also some planned features:
Integer ranges as types.
Generics with traits
Clock domain information on types.
Mixing domains without explicit synchronization is a compilation error.
Related: clock domain inference where the domain is obvious.
And more...
Using Spade
To get started, read the (work in progress)
spade book
.
For an overview of what Spade is, have a look at this
talk from OSDA 2023
.
Documentation is very much a work in progress, but some is available in our
book
.
Spade is in its early stages, so everything is subject to change. You can build
things with it but be prepared for bugs and missing features.
Learn more
Feel free to follow the development either on
Gitlab
or in

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：连续血糖监测（CGM）的有效性及其在不同个体中血糖反应的差异

不同观点：
• **pedalpete** 认为血糖不仅受饮食影响，还受睡眠质量、肠道菌群、激素变化等多种因素的影响。这些因素使得CGM更有价值，因为它可以帮助持续管理血糖，而非一次性检查。
• **csours** 强调了基于证据的医学（EBM）的重要性，指出虽然有些常识可能是显而易见的，但仍需要科学证据支持。同时，EBM在个性化治疗方面的不足也被提出批评。
• **utopcell** 分享了个人使用CGM的经验，认为CGM提供了对自身状态的意识，并强调了个体对食物反应的差异性，例如对可乐和菲达奶酪的不同反应。
• **blindriver** 是一位2型糖尿病患者，分享了其CGM使用体验，质疑自己是否真的患有T2D，因为血糖反应与传统认知不符，并认为CGM揭示了糖尿病的多样性。
• **taeric** 和 **jzacharia** 都提到活动水平、饥饿状态、压力、激素等多因素对血糖反应的影响，认为这些因素导致血糖反应难以复制。
• **slwvx** 引用了Jessie Inchauspe的工作，提到饮食顺序和运动对血糖反应的影响，并提供了具体的饮食建议。
• **aucisson_masque** 讨论了副交感/交感神经系统及饮食顺序对血糖反应的影响，指出即使食物在胃中混合，顺序依然重要。
• **stranded22** 分享了其T1D妻子的经历，强调了血糖管理的复杂性和挫败感。
• **francisofascii** 和 **siliconc0w** 则认为CGM反映的个体差异是预期内的，并提到已知的如时间、运动、食物成分等对血糖反应的影响。
• **FollowingTheDao** 希望研究同时检测胰岛素反应，以获得更全面的理解。
• **ggandv** 关注研究中提到的80%的变异可能来源于个体差异或测量误差。

补充讨论：
• CGM的个性化管理价值：多个评论强调CGM在个性化血糖管理中的重要性，而非一次性诊断工具。
• 个体差异：多个评论指出，不同个体对相同食物的反应差异显著，强调了饮食管理的复杂性。
• EBM的局限性：csours指出EBM在个性化治疗和理解不同干预效果方面的不足。
• 饮食顺序和活动的影响：多个评论提到饮食顺序、运动等因素对血糖反应的影响，这与传统认知有所不同。
• 测量误差和研究局限：一些评论关注研究中的变异可能来源于测量误差，提示研究结果的解释需谨慎。

争议焦点：
• CGM数据的解释和应用：不同评论者对CGM数据的解释存在不同看法，一些人认为CGM揭示了血糖管理的复杂性，而另一些人则认为这是预期内的结果。
• EBM和常识之间的平衡：csours指出，虽然有些常识是显而易见的，但仍需科学证据支持，这在医学实践中可能导致不同的理解和应用。

data.article_summary: 美国联邦贸易委员会（FTC）将原定于5月14日生效的“点击取消”规则 enforcement 推迟至7月14日。该规则要求订阅服务的取消流程必须与其注册流程一样简便，例如如果注册可以在线完成，那么取消也必须可以在线进行。此次延期是由于对企业在原定日期前 compliance 的负担进行了重新评估，FTC 以3-0的投票结果通过了延期决定。不过，FTC 表示在新截止日期后将严格执行该规则，但不排除在执行过程中根据暴露的问题对规则进行修改。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：消费者在取消服务时遇到的困难和不便，以及相关监管和企业行为的讨论。

不同观点：
• [arwhatever] 描述了自己试图取消DSL服务时的糟糕体验，包括口音难以理解的客服、反复的电话转接和长时间的等待。他认为这种拖延策略增加了企业的利润，激励了不良商业行为。
• [RankingMember] 认为这种 cancellations 被故意拖延是荒谬的，但在此类管理下并不令人惊讶。
• [tantalor] 指出，在考虑消费者可能受到的损害时，强制合规的负担被忽略了。
• [sillystu04] 认为Visa/Mastercard有能力自行执行更严格的措施，但更希望通过监管实现。他建议通过公开信和媒体报道可能会促使这些公司采取行动。
• [nixpulvis] 希望有候选人以消费者保护为主要竞选纲领，因为公司越来越不受约束。
• [SoftTalker] 提到如果可以在线订阅，那么取消订阅也应当同样方便，但担心取消选项可能被隐藏在网站的 obscure 部分。
• [OptionOfT] 认为服务通常是先收费后使用，因此如果无法收费就可以立即取消访问。他批评公司通过获取大量用户信息使得取消服务变得极其困难。

补充讨论：
• [bilsbie] 表示因为取消服务的麻烦而避免加入某些服务，并拒绝使用免费试用。

• [Suppafly] 认为在共和党执政期间，亲消费者的政策往往被取消或推迟。
• [kylehotchkiss] 提到当前政府的选民本可以从消费者保护政策中受益，但企业却采取了反消费者的立场。
• [typedef_struct] 提出“点击收费”的概念，即如果用户不主动点击使用服务，公司就不能收费。
• [Gud] 作为欧洲人，对美国消费者在取消服务时面临的困难表示惊讶。
• [bee_rider] 认为由于 dark patterns 和不良商业行为，现在的互联网环境变得 hostile 和 manipulative，使得消费者不愿意支付费用。

争议焦点：
• 消费者在取消服务时面临的障碍和不便，以及企业是否有意识地利用这些障碍来增加利润。
• 政府监管和企业自律之间的平衡，如何有效保护消费者权益。
• 不同政治背景对消费者保护政策的影响。

43962528.article_content:
News
The FTC puts off enforcing its ‘click-to-cancel’ rule
Companies now have until July 14th to make it as easy to cancel subscriptions as it is to sign up for them.
Companies now have until July 14th to make it as easy to cancel subscriptions as it is to sign up for them.
by
Wes Davis
May 10, 2025, 10:14 PM UTC
Link
Facebook
Threads
The FTC seal.
Image: Cath Virginia / The Verge
Wes Davis
is a weekend editor who covers the latest in tech and entertainment. He has written news, reviews, and more as a tech journalist since 2020.
The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) was set to start enforcing the remaining provisions of its “click-to-cancel” rule on May 14th, requiring that subscriptions be as easy to cancel as to start. Now,
the agency says
it won’t enforce the rule until July 14th, as
TechCrunch
reports
.
Also known as the Negative Option Rule, the big component of click-to-cancel is that it forbids companies from making customers jump through hoops that differ from the process to sign up for an account. If you can sign up online, you must be able to cancel online, too. As the FTC points out, the original May 14th deadline was already a deferral for that and related provisions.
Related
The FTC is finally making it easier to cancel your gym membership
Guess who’s suing the FTC to stop ‘click to cancel’
The agency says it chose to push enforcement back even further after “a fresh assessment of the burdens that forcing compliance by this date would impose.” The FTC voted 3-0 for the delay, but as
TechCrunch
notes, two of a typical five commissioners were absent from the vote. That’s because they were
illegally fired by Donald Trump
in March.
Perhaps on the bright side for consumers, the FTC says that starting on the new deadline, “regulated entities must be in compliance with the whole of the Rule because the Commission will begin enforcing it.” However, it doesn’t rule out changing any of the regulation’s provisions, writing that it’s “open to amending the Rule” if enforcing it “exposes any problems.”

主要讨论点：Hacker News (HN) 用户对平台前端体验的改进建议和替代方案。

不同观点：
• [yathern] 介绍了自己的HN替代前端 https://hn.zip，其特点是预缓存首页帖子，方便在网络不稳定的情况下浏览评论，尤其在地铁中使用。
• [canucker2016] 分享了自己通过JavaScript增强HN体验的经历，如高亮新评论和优化评论浏览效率，但后来被其他新事物分心。
• [thegrim33] 希望有一个扩展可以自动过滤政治/社会内容以及情绪化争论，通过AI情感分析自动屏蔽不符合要求的用户评论和提交的内容，只保留技术和科学相关内容。
• [anonu] 建议HN增加分类标签以帮助找到感兴趣的帖子，并希望通过Chrome扩展实现，而无需记住新网站。
• [insin] 开发了一个扩展来解决重复访问时难以跟随评论线程的问题，并提供了其他移动端优化功能。同时也提到正在开发跨设备同步后端。
• [alabhyajindal] 创建了一个浏览器扩展，可以根据用户提供的关键词隐藏帖子，并获得了积极的用户反馈。
• [Suppafly] 质疑是否因为用户使用替代前端导致HN的基础体验没有得到改进，或者这是为了保持新手难以融入。
• [Yizahi] 推荐了另一个替代前端 https://hckrnews.com。
• [smusamashah] 提供了一个用户脚本，通过localStorage标记新故事和评论，帮助用户追踪错过的内容。
• [fiveleavesleft] 提到开发了一些工具来提高HN浏览效率，但没有详细说明。
• [MinimalAction] 表示自己也遇到多标签页管理问题，但不同意通过推送通知（如Telegram）来解决问题，认为应该更注意管理阅读时间。
• [0x008] 推荐了另一个项目 https://github.com/simonw/llm-hacker-news。
• [DerCommodore] 分享了自己开发的HN阅读器 https://www.hn-reader.com，包括AI总结、推送通知、保存到列表和滑动操作等功能。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是如何有效管理HN上的大量评论和内容，部分用户如[thegrim33]希望通过自动过滤来避免政治和社会内容，而[yathern]和[insin]则专注于技术解决方案如预缓存和高亮新评论。
• 用户对基础体验的改进存在不同看法，[Suppafly]提出是否因为替代前端导致基础平台未得到改进，而[MinimalAction]则对推送通知持反对态度，认为这会干扰专注。
• 多个用户分享了自己开发的工具和扩展，如[alabhyajindal]的关键词过滤扩展、[insin]的评论高亮和折叠扩展、以及[DerCommodore]的AI阅读器。

总体来看，讨论围绕如何通过技术手段提升HN的用户体验，包括过滤内容、优化评论浏览和改进移动端使用效率等。

data.title: Gig Companies Violate Workers Rights
data.author: Improvement
data.article_summary: 根据人权观察（Human Rights Watch）2025年发布的报告《陷阱：美国平台工作中的算法、工资和劳动剥削》，美国主要数字劳工平台（如Amazon Flex、DoorDash、Uber等）将零工工人错误分类为独立承包商，剥夺其劳动权益。这些公司使用不透明的算法分配工作并决定工资，导致工人在完成工作前无法得知收入。工人们往往赚取低于最低工资的收入，且面临不稳定的工资和工作随时被终止的风险。由于平台算法不透明，工人难以挑战有关其工作或工资的决定。此外，工人还需自行承担车辆、保险等费用，进一步加剧经济不安全感。尽管这些公司市值巨大，但工人们仍面临低工资和缺乏社会保障的困境。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： gig经济中的劳动者权益和平台责任分配问题

不同观点：
• **[adocomplete]** 认为Uber等平台在车费分配中拿走了过高的比例，司机承担了所有的工作和车辆损耗，但收入不到总费用的一半，这种分配不合理。
• **[n_ary]** 指出，gig经济中的劳动者往往为了生计不敢对平台提出异议，因为他们处于绝望的境地，而平台则掌握了绝大多数的议价权，这种权力失衡很难改变。
• **[flkiwi]** 强调gig公司对劳动者权利的漠视，平台在出现问题时总是推卸责任，且消费者缺乏有效的投诉渠道。但同时也提到一些公司开始推出更负责任的服务模式。
• **[ApolloFortyNine]** 认为平台算法的不透明是当前最需要解决的问题，虽然Uber已经显示了收入预估，但无法强制要求用户只接受 profitable 的订单。同时，劳动者有权选择通过缩短车辆寿命来换取当前收入。
• **[econ]** 提出应消除员工和企业家之间的区别，建议设定不同级别的最低工资，允许雇主通过支付费用来放弃某些福利，以激励短期合同的灵活性。
• **[SirMaster]** 认为gig工作本就不应被视为全职工作，这正是gig经济的初衷。
• **[ProllyInfamous]** 分享了自己在gig平台上的负面经历，指出平台对劳动者的不公平对待，并表示这种情况可能至今仍未改善。

补充讨论：
• **[breakyerself]** 希望有一些非营利版本的gig平台。
• **[Extropy_]** 提出了“gig工作是否应被视为正式雇佣”的问题。
• **[guiriduro] 和 [qmr]** 的评论带有讽刺意味，对讨论中的某些显而易见的问题进行了调侃。

争议焦点：
• gig经济中平台与劳动者之间的收入分配不均。
• 平台对劳动者权利的漠视和问题责任的推卸。
• 是否应通过立法或其他方式增加平台算法的透明度和公平性。

总体来看，讨论围绕gig经济中劳动者权益、收入分配及平台责任展开，不同参与者从各自经验和视角出发，提出了对现状的批评和改进建议。

Human Rights Watch
US: Major Companies Violate Gig Workers’ Rights
Print
Donate Now
Click to expand Image
© 2025 Brian Stauffer for Human Rights Watch
(Washington, DC) – Major digital labor platforms, also known as gig companies, operating in the
United States
misclassify gig workers as independent contractors, denying them labor rights, Human Rights Watch said in a report released today.
The 155-page
report
, “‘The Gig Trap’: Algorithmic, Wage and Labor Exploitation in Platform Work in the US” focuses on seven major companies operating in the US: Amazon Flex, DoorDash, Favor, Instacart, Lyft, Shipt, and Uber. These companies claim to offer gig workers “flexibility” but often end up paying them less than state or local minimum wages. Six of the seven companies use algorithms with opaque rules to assign jobs and determine wages, meaning that workers do not know how much they will be paid until after completing the job.
May 12, 2025
The Gig Trap
Algorithmic, Wage and Labor Exploitation in Platform Work in the US
Download the full report in English
Human Rights Watch correspondence with digital labor platforms, 2022
Human Rights Watch correspondence with digital labor platforms, March 2025
Human Rights Watch correspondence with digital labor platforms, April 2025
Human Rights Watch correspondence with digital labor platforms, May 2025
Human Rights Watch correspondence with government agencies, April 2025
“Digital labor platforms have created a business model that evades employer responsibilities while keeping workers under tight algorithmic control, driven by opaque and unpredictable decisions,” said
Lena Simet
, senior researcher on poverty and inequality at Human Rights Watch. “They promise flexibility but, in reality, they leave workers at the mercy of unstable and subminimum wages, little social protection, and in constant fear of termination without recourse.”
Workers for the seven platforms examined are assigned orders, supervised, paid, and fired by algorithms. All except Amazon Flex, which uses a flat hourly wage, use opaque and frequently changing algorithms to calculate pay per job or shift. Apps and platforms are designed to keep gig workers on the job for long hours and low pay, and dynamic pricing algorithms make it extremely difficult for them to plan their schedules and manage their earnings. Managed by algorithms, workers cannot fully understand how they are assigned work, or how their wages are calculated. Without any transparency, it’s extremely difficult for them to challenge decisions made about their work or pay.
Human Rights Watch examined the working conditions of ride-hailing, shopping, and food delivery workers, with a focus on Texas. The report is based on semi-structured interviews with 95 platform workers in Texas and 12 other US states, as well as a survey of 127 workers in Texas.
Low wages, algorithmic control and barriers to unionizing trap many workers in economic insecurity, even as multi-billion-dollar companies expand their market share and revenue, Human Rights Watch found.
Weak regulations allow these companies to misclassify workers as independent contractors rather than employees, despite the nature of the work and degree of control exercised by the companies often meeting legal criteria for employee status. This enables companies to avoid compliance with minimum wage laws, overtime pay, and contributions to nonwage benefits. For workers, it means providing their own vehicles, fuel, insurance, and maintenance as well as paying the employer’s share of Social Security and Medicare contributions.
The Texas workers surveyed earned nearly 30 percent below the federal minimum wage and about 70 percent below what the Massachusetts Institute of Technology estimates is a living wage in Texas. These findings reinforce those of
local governments
,
academic institutions
, and
policy researchers
, who have consistently found that these workers earn at or below local minimum wages and well below the thresholds needed for a decent standard of living.
The US is home to one of the largest global markets for digital platform work, and the number of people earning income from gig work has surged in recent years.
Estimates suggest that by 2021
, 16 percent of US adults had worked for a digital labor platform at least once. Platform workers are disproportionately Black or Latinx and live in lower income households.
Workers who responded to the Human Rights Watch survey received an average of US$16.90 per hour (including tips), but nearly half of that was spent on work-related expenses. After accounting for nonwage benefits that employers often cover for other workers, their effective pay fell to $5.12 per hour. Some workers reported earning nothing at all after expenses.

data.title: Show HN: CLI that spots fake GitHub stars, risky dependencies and licence traps
data.author: artski
data.article_summary: StarGuard是一款CLI工具，旨在检测GitHub仓库中的虚假星标活动、依赖劫持、许可证风险等开源风险。它通过分析星标异常、依赖文件、许可证类型以及代码信号，生成信任评分，帮助CTO、安全团队和投资人快速进行开源项目的尽职调查。该工具提供多种输出格式和可视化图表，支持自动化扫描和集成，具备高效、可扩展的特点。StarGuard使用公共元数据，不存储个人信息，确保安全与隐私。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GitHub项目中机器人账户检测的策略及相关问题

不同观点：
• [the__alchemist] 认为如果一个项目的90%提交来自一个几个月没更新的人，这只是轻微的绿色警告，而非红色警告。
• [coffeeboy] 支持这种检测策略，并补充了两个额外的启发式方法：1. Fork与star的比例，通常比例不会超过0.5；2. 假仓库所有者会直接克隆真实项目并推送到自己账户，冒充真实项目。
• [hungryhobbit] 质疑项目为何需要同时使用Python、Java、Go和Ruby等多种语言，认为这可能不必要。
• [sesm] 提出如何区分自然增长的star和非自然增长的star，例如通过Hacker News等平台的宣传带来的star。
• [ngangaga] 认为GitHub的star没有信号质量，不应影响招聘决策、投资条款和依赖选择，觉得这种现象很荒谬。
• [binary132] 建议 heuristics 应该是可定制和透明的，以便用户可以根据具体情况选择或查看报告。
• [zxilly] 怀疑项目的代码是AI生成的，指出代码中的多个问题，如hallucinatory描述、冗长的函数名、被注释掉的函数等，认为代码质量需要改进。
• [knowitnone] 认为这种机器人检测应该由GitHub自己来做，并对GitHub没有因提供恶意软件而被起诉感到惊讶。
• [nfriedly] 提出将此项目转化为浏览器扩展的可行性问题。
• [feverzsj] 指出CTO们不关心GitHub的star，因为他们依赖于严格的筛选过程。
• [edoceo] 询问是否可以通过package.json添加PHP支持，并提出是否接受补丁。
• [Am4TIfIsER0ppos] 询问什么是license trap，例如AGPL伪装成MIT许可证是否只是普通的许可证违规。
• [nottorp] 认为GitHub可以去掉star功能，或者用户自己研究依赖项，而不是依赖star。

补充讨论：
• 项目代码质量问题和AI生成代码的争议是讨论的一个焦点，[zxilly] 提出了详细的代码问题。
• 不同用户对star的价值和项目检测策略有不同看法，[ngangaga] 和 [the__alchemist] 对star的意义有不同理解。
• 关于如何改进检测策略和工具的实用性，[coffeeboy]、[binary132] 和 [nfriedly] 提出了具体建议和扩展想法。

⭐ StarGuard: Trust Scores for GitHub Repositories
CLI tool
to detect fake-star campaigns, dependency hijacks, licence red flags, and other signals of open-source risk.
Inspired by the
4.5 million fake stars study
, StarGuard helps
CTOs, security teams, and VCs
automate open-source due diligence in seconds.
📌 Why StarGuard?
Fake stars are rampant.
Research shows botnets and paid campaigns artificially inflate repo popularity.
Supply chain attacks are rising.
Malicious packages and licence traps easily reach production.
Manual review doesn’t scale.

43962427.article_summary: StarGuard是一款CLI工具，旨在检测GitHub仓库中的虚假星标活动、依赖劫持、许可证风险等开源风险。它通过分析星标异常、依赖文件、许可证类型以及代码信号，生成信任评分，帮助CTO、安全团队和投资人快速进行开源项目的尽职调查。该工具提供多种输出格式和可视化图表，支持自动化扫描和集成，具备高效、可扩展的特点。StarGuard使用公共元数据，不存储个人信息，确保安全与隐私。
43962427.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GitHub项目中机器人账户检测的策略及相关问题

不同观点：
• [the__alchemist] 认为如果一个项目的90%提交来自一个几个月没更新的人，这只是轻微的绿色警告，而非红色警告。
• [coffeeboy] 支持这种检测策略，并补充了两个额外的启发式方法：1. Fork与star的比例，通常比例不会超过0.5；2. 假仓库所有者会直接克隆真实项目并推送到自己账户，冒充真实项目。
• [hungryhobbit] 质疑项目为何需要同时使用Python、Java、Go和Ruby等多种语言，认为这可能不必要。
• [sesm] 提出如何区分自然增长的star和非自然增长的star，例如通过Hacker News等平台的宣传带来的star。
• [ngangaga] 认为GitHub的star没有信号质量，不应影响招聘决策、投资条款和依赖选择，觉得这种现象很荒谬。
• [binary132] 建议 heuristics 应该是可定制和透明的，以便用户可以根据具体情况选择或查看报告。
• [zxilly] 怀疑项目的代码是AI生成的，指出代码中的多个问题，如hallucinatory描述、冗长的函数名、被注释掉的函数等，认为代码质量需要改进。
• [knowitnone] 认为这种机器人检测应该由GitHub自己来做，并对GitHub没有因提供恶意软件而被起诉感到惊讶。
• [nfriedly] 提出将此项目转化为浏览器扩展的可行性问题。
• [feverzsj] 指出CTO们不关心GitHub的star，因为他们依赖于严格的筛选过程。
• [edoceo] 询问是否可以通过package.json添加PHP支持，并提出是否接受补丁。
• [Am4TIfIsER0ppos] 询问什么是license trap，例如AGPL伪装成MIT许可证是否只是普通的许可证违规。
• [nottorp] 认为GitHub可以去掉star功能，或者用户自己研究依赖项，而不是依赖star。

补充讨论：
• 项目代码质量问题和AI生成代码的争议是讨论的一个焦点，[zxilly] 提出了详细的代码问题。
• 不同用户对star的价值和项目检测策略有不同看法，[ngangaga] 和 [the__alchemist] 对star的意义有不同理解。
• 关于如何改进检测策略和工具的实用性，[coffeeboy]、[binary132] 和 [nfriedly] 提出了具体建议和扩展想法。

不同观点：

data.author: ibobev
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于计算机图形学（CG）论文的讨论，尤其是针对隐式几何体生成一致性UV贴图的算法及其应用问题。

不同观点：
• Remnant44：对该论文的时机和内容表示赞赏。他认为论文概念和实现结合得很好，且很高兴看到一篇不涉及神经网络或AI生成技术的CG论文，带来了一些新鲜感。
• whizzter：认为该论文对处理隐式表面的人很有趣，但需要时间消化。他指出论文缺乏UV贴图结果的具体示例，并质疑如果隐式模型的结构发生变化，UV贴图是否能保持相似性或可转移性。他还提到，隐式表面建模工具发展迅速，论文中未涉及如何与创作工具结合的问题。
• kaoD：关心如何解决使用SDF（符号距离函数）进行表面位移时出现的可见不连续性问题，特别是在进行光线行进渲染时。他提到表面函数不再满足Eikonal方程，并询问是否有解决方案。
• jplusequalt：对论文表示高度赞赏，认为这是计算机图形学中非常有趣的一个例子，展示了该领域的吸引力。

补充讨论：
• whizzter对隐式表面建模工具的快速演变表示关注，并提出UV贴图在模型结构变化时的处理问题，特别举例两个独立球体平滑连接时UV贴图的合并情况。
• kaoD的具体技术问题涉及到数学和SDF的正确性，特别是如何修复不满足Eikonal方程的表面函数，显示了理论与实践结合的挑战。
• 争议焦点可能在于隐式几何体建模工具和UV贴图生成算法的实际应用效果和可操作性，尤其是在模型结构变化时的UV贴图处理问题上。

这些讨论反映了计算机图形学领域中理论研究与实际应用之间的张力，以及不同从业者对工具和算法实用性的关注。

data.title: Creating a static website for all my bookmarks
data.author: paulcapewell
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者将所有书签迁移到一个静态网站的经历和原因。作者曾使用Pinboard管理书签，但由于该网站逐渐被弃用且出现各种问题，作者决定转向使用本地静态网站来管理书签。静态网站不需要依赖在线服务，作者可以更好地控制数据，并且无需担心服务被关闭。作者的静态书签网站主要是一个包含所有链接的滚动列表，每个书签都有标题、URL、手写摘要和标签列表。作者认为手写摘要更有助于记忆和回顾，并且静态网站的灵活性和可移植性很高。本文是关于书签系列的第一篇，后续将探讨书签管理的原因、静态网站的优势以及构建个人网络档案的经验。

43960470.article_content:
Creating a static website for all my bookmarks
Tagged with
bookmarking
,
static sites
Posted
12 May 2025
I’m storing more and more of my data
as static websites
, and about a year ago I switched to using a local, static site to manage my bookmarks. It’s replaced
Pinboard
as the way I track interesting links and cool web pages. I save articles I’ve read, talks I’ve watched, fanfiction I’ve enjoyed.
It’s taken hundreds of hours to get all my bookmarks and saved web pages into this new site, and it’s taught me a lot about archiving and building the web. This post is the first of a four-part series about my bookmarks, and I’ll publish the rest of the series over the next three weeks.
Bookmarking mini-series
Creating a static site for all my bookmarks
(this article)
Why do I bookmark?
Why use a static website?
What does it look like?
How does it work?
How I built a personal archive of the web
(coming 19 May) – how I built a web archive by hand, the tradeoffs between manual and automated archiving, and what I learnt about preserving the web.
What I learnt about building websites by reading two thousand web pages
(coming 26 May) – how to write thoughtful HTML, new-to-me features of CSS, and some quirks and relics I found while building my personal web archive.
Some cool websites from my bookmark collection
(coming 2 June) – my favorite sites I rediscovered while reviewing my bookmarks. Fun, creative corners of the web that make me smile.
Why do I bookmark?
I bookmark because I want to find links later
Keeping my own list of bookmarks means that I can always find old links. If I have a vague memory of a web page, I’m more likely to find it in my bookmarks than in the vast ocean of the web. Links rot, websites break, and a lot of what I read isn’t indexed by Google.
This is particularly true for fannish creations. A lot of fan artists deliberately publish in closed communities, so their work is only visible to like-minded fans, and not something that a casual Internet user might stumble upon. If I’m looking for an exact story I read five years ago, I’m far more likely to find it in my bookmarks than by scouring the Internet.
Finding old web pages has always been hard, and the rise of generative AI has made it even harder. Search results are full of AI slop, and people are trying to hide their content from scrapers. Locking the web behind paywalls and registration screens might protect it from scrapers, but it also makes it
harder to find
.
I bookmark to remember why I liked a link
I write notes on each bookmark I keep, so I remember why a particular link was fun or interesting.
When I save articles, I write a short summary of the key points, information, arguments. I can review a one paragraph summary much faster than I can reread the entire page.
When I save fanfiction, I write notes on the plot or key moments. Is this the story where they live happily ever after? Or does this have a gut wrenching ending that needs a box of tissues?
These summaries could be farmed out to generative AI, but I much prefer writing them myself. I can phrase things in my own words, write down connections to other ideas, and write a more personal summary than I get from a machine. And when I read those summaries back later, I remember writing them, and it revives my memories of the original article or story. It’s slower, but I find it much more useful.
Why use a static website?
I was a happy
Pinboard
customer for over a decade, but the site
feels abandoned
. I’ve not had catastrophic errors, but I kept running into broken features or rough edges – search timeouts, unreliable archiving, unexpected outages. There does seem to be some renewed activity in the last few months, but it was too late – I’d already moved away.
I briefly considered Pinboard alternatives like
Raindrop
,
Pocket
and
Instapaper
– but I’d still be trusting an online service. I’ve been burned too many times by services being abandoned, and so I’ve gradually been moving the data I care about to
static websites
on my local machine. It takes a bit of work to set up, but then I have more control and I’m not worried about it going away.
My needs are pretty simple – I just want a list of links, some basic filtering and search, and a saved copy of all my links. I don’t need social features or integrations, which made it easier to walk away from Pinboard.
I’ve been using static sites for all sorts of data, and I’m enjoying the flexibility and portability of vanilla HTML and JavaScript. They need minimal maintenance and there’s no lock-in, and I’ve made enough of them now that I can
create new ones
pretty quickly.
What does it look like?
The main page is a scrolling list of all my bookmarks. This is a single page that shows every link, because my collection is small enough that I don’t need pagination.
Each bookmark has a title, a URL, my hand-written summary, and a list of tags.
If I’m looking for a specific bookmark, I can filter by tag or by author, or I can use my browser’s i
43960470.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者将所有书签迁移到一个静态网站的经历和原因。作者曾使用Pinboard管理书签，但由于该网站逐渐被弃用且出现各种问题，作者决定转向使用本地静态网站来管理书签。静态网站不需要依赖在线服务，作者可以更好地控制数据，并且无需担心服务被关闭。作者的静态书签网站主要是一个包含所有链接的滚动列表，每个书签都有标题、URL、手写摘要和标签列表。作者认为手写摘要更有助于记忆和回顾，并且静态网站的灵活性和可移植性很高。本文是关于书签系列的第一篇，后续将探讨书签管理的原因、静态网站的优势以及构建个人网络档案的经验。

data.title: Have you ever seen an emolument fly?
data.author: treetalker
data.article_summary: ABC News报道，特朗普政府计划接受卡塔尔皇室赠送的一架波音747-8豪华飞机，该飞机将被用作总统专机直至特朗普卸任，之后将转交给特朗普总统图书馆基金会。白宫和司法部的律师认为，该赠予不违反反贿赂法或宪法关于接受外国礼物的禁令，因为飞机将先赠予美国空军，之后再转给图书馆基金会。同时，特朗普家族公司还被报道与卡塔尔签署了建造豪华度假村的协议，尽管这引发了对其利用总统职位获取个人经济利益的担忧。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于政府资金用于翻新飞机并捐赠给特朗普图书馆基金会是否合理，以及相关政治影响的讨论。

不同观点：
• [rbanffy] 认为，使用政府资金两次翻新飞机，然后将其捐赠给特朗普图书馆基金会是不合理的。他质疑一所图书馆为何需要一架波音747，并认为这非常荒谬。

• [AIPedant] 将此问题与萨尔瓦多的政治状况进行类比，认为卡塔尔王室通过迎合特朗普对法治的蔑视正在犯下严重错误。他担心这种行为会导致美国宪法秩序被破坏，并使卡塔尔被视为通过贿赂影响美国总统。

• [treetalker] 对安全问题持不同看法，认为由Hegseth领导的国防部能够确保飞机的安全，不会被泄露。他还指出，在特朗普任期结束前将卡塔尔“捐赠”的飞机转移到特朗普总统图书馆基金会，可以有效避免下一届政府对飞机的使用和安全审查。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于政府资金的使用是否合理，以及这种捐赠行为是否带有政治目的和潜在的安全隐患。
• [AIPedant] 强调了这种行为对国际关系和法治的负面影响，而[treetalker] 则更关注飞机的安全和转移时机的政治考虑。
• [rbanffy] 的评论则主要聚焦在捐赠行为的合理性和必要性问题，特别是对资源使用的质疑。

The Volokh Conspiracy
Mostly law professors | Sometimes contrarian | Often libertarian | Always independent
About The Volokh Conspiracy
Editorial Independence
Who we are
Books
Volokh Daily Email
Archives
DMCA

ABC News
reports
:
In what may be the most valuable gift ever extended to the United States from a foreign government, the Trump administration is preparing to accept a super luxury Boeing 747-8 jumbo jet from the royal family of Qatar -- a gift that is to be available for use by President Donald Trump as the new Air Force One until shortly before he leaves office, at which time ownership of the plane will be transferred to the Trump presidential library foundation, sources familiar with the proposed arrangement told ABC News.
The gift is expected to be announced next week, when Trump visits Qatar on the first foreign trip of his second term, according to sources familiar with the plans.
Trump toured the plane, which is so opulently configured it is known as "a flying palace," while it was parked at the West Palm Beach International Airport in February.
One might think this gift raises legal issues. Administration lawyers apparently have those bases covered:
sources told ABC News that lawyers for the White House counsel's office and the Department of Justice drafted an analysis for Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth concluding that is legal for the Department of Defense to accept the aircraft as a gift and later turn it over to the Trump library, and that it does not violate laws against bribery or the Constitution's prohibition (the emoluments clause) of any U.S. government official accepting gifts "from any King, Prince or foreign State."
Sources told ABC News that Attorney General Pam Bondi and Trump's top White House lawyer David Warrington concluded it would be "legally permissible" for the donation of the aircraft to be conditioned on transferring its ownership to Trump's presidential library before the end of his term, according to sources familiar with their determination. . . .
Both the White House and DOJ concluded that because the gift is not conditioned on any official act, it does not constitute bribery, the sources said. Bondi's legal analysis also says it does not run afoul of the Constitution's prohibition on foreign gifts because the plane is not being given to an individual, but rather to the United States Air Force and, eventually, to the presidential library foundation, the sources said.
One might also think a gift of this sort could raise security concerns, particularly given the Qatari government's
efforts to influence U.S. policy
(and
universities
). Apparently such concerns will be addressed when the plane is modified to meet the requirements for presidential use.
According to the story, the plane is to be transferred to the Trump Presidential Library Foundation no later than January 1, 2029, at the federal government's expense. The story estimates the value of the plane at approximately $400 million.
In unrelated news, the Associated Press
reported
on April 30:
The Trump family company struck a deal Wednesday to build a luxury golf resort in Qatar in a sign it has no plans to hold back from foreign dealmaking during a second Trump administration, despite the danger of a president shaping U.S. public policy for personal financial gain.
The project, which features Trump-branded beachside villas and an 18-hole golf course to be built by a Saudi Arabian company, is the first foreign deal by the Trump Organization since Donald Trump took office and unlike any done in his first term. Back then, he forswore foreign deals in an extraordinary press conference surrounded by stacks of legal documents as he pledged to avoid even the appearance of conflict of interest.

data.title: Show HN: Blog comments, nice looking, open source – Talkyard
data.author: KajMagnus
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了如何在博客中嵌入Talkyard评论功能。通过在网页中添加特定JavaScript代码，并确保论坛配置允许从该域嵌入，即可实现评论功能。文章提供了代码示例，并说明可以将Talkyard用作论坛嵌入，但目前存在一些问题，如页面重载时用户会从嵌入的论坛中登出（博客评论则无此问题）。文章还提到评论实际上来自另一篇博客，此处仅作展示用途。用户可以在论坛中报告任何发现的bug。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对讨论系统的评价与建议

不同观点：
• [imiric] 赞赏该系统对讨论质量的重视，特别是区分了“点赞”和“不同意”的功能。他认为这有助于更细致地表达对评论的看法，而不应像现有平台（如Reddit）那样将两者混用。
• [imiric] 同时表达了对Slashdot投票系统的偏好，认为其对投票进行分类（如“有信息价值”、“有洞察力”、“离题”等）以及限制用户投票数量的机制，能够进一步提升讨论质量。

补充讨论：
• [imiric] 指出了该系统页面存在的一些技术问题，例如定价页面上的拼写错误（"commets"应为"comments"），以及旧计划链接返回404错误。他建议对页面内容进行全面修订，并移除所有标有“稍后添加”的功能，以提升用户体验。

争议焦点：
• 目前点赞和不同意的混用问题：[imiric]认为点赞和不同意是两个独立的维度，但在现有平台上往往被混为一谈，这是一个需要改进的方面。
• 对不同讨论系统优劣的看法：[imiric]更倾向于Slashdot的投票系统，因其具有更细致的分类和限制机制，而当前讨论系统尽管有所改进，但仍有提升空间。

• 目前点赞和不同意的混用问题：[imiric]认为点赞和不同意是两个独立的维度，但在现有平台上往往被混为一谈，这是一个需要改进的方面。
• 对不同讨论系统优劣的看法：[imiric]更倾向于Slashdot的投票系统，因其具有更细致的分类和限制机制，而当前讨论系统尽管有所改进，但仍有提升空间。

不同观点：
• MacNCheese23认为，基于TCP的WebSocket和JSON消息解析与典型的MMORPG通信架构不同。他指出，MMORPG通常使用无损/重试/防故障的基于UDP的协议来处理网络层，因为这是MMO架构中最难的部分。他还提到，有很多示例库可以参考，并建议查看索尼在线娱乐（SW Online）泄露的代码以了解其实现。

• MJGrzymek提出了一个具体的浏览器错误问题，他在使用Android版的Chrome访问everwilds.io时遇到了SSL证书错误（net::ERR_CERT_COMMON_NAME_INVALID）。这个评论更偏向于技术实现中的实际问题，而非架构设计。

• ricardobayes表达了对MMORPG中运动和相机系统的用户体验的看法。他认为迄今为止没有任何MMORPG在运动和相机系统的流畅性上能超越《魔兽世界》（WoW）。

Everwilds
Everwilds is a prototype and reference project that demonstrates how MMORPGs
like World of Warcraft are programmed, focusing primarily on networking and
netcode architecture. It serves as a learning resource for developers interested
in how real-time online RPGs handle networking, synchronization, and
client-server interaction.
😊
Why?
Ever since I was a kid playing the original Guild Wars and World of Warcraft,
I’ve wanted to learn how those kinds of games are made. That curiosity sparked
my interest in programming and game development. This project is the result of
deciding to dig deep into the architecture and technical foundations of
large-scale online games.
🧪 What's Included
While this is not a full MMORPG, it includes:
A working client-server architecture
Character movement with walk animation
A basic combat system
A simple leveling system (up to level 10)
A chat system
The highlight of this project is its approach to player movement synchronization
between clients. It uses the same technique used by World of Warcraft, enabling
smooth movement replication with minimal bandwidth usage, and allowing
scalability for many concurrent players. While the general method is publicly
known, implementing it correctly took a bit of research, trial and error, and
digging through obscure forums and private server codebases.
🚀 Technologies Used
Three.js
TypeScript
HTML/CSS
🛠️ Installation
To run Everwilds locally execute the following commands in your terminal:
$ git clone https://github.com/nickyvanurk/everwilds
$
cd
./everwilds
$ npm i
$ npm run build
$ npm start
On Windows you have to manually copy the client/assets folder to the dist
folder, as the build command uses a Linux command that doesn't work on Windows.
If everything went well the game will be available at
http://localhost:3000

data.title: Replacing tmux and GNU screen with Emacs
data.author: signa11
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了从使用终端复用器（如GNU screen或tmux）转向Emacs作为替代方案的可能性。对于已经使用Emacs的用户，Emacs几乎可以完成终端复用器的所有功能，包括会话的 detach 和 re-attach、窗口管理、终端模拟和运行shell等。文章指出，虽然在远程服务器或没有Emacs的环境中，tmux仍有其必要性，但对于习惯命令行的用户，Emacs提供了更强大的功能和更少的键位冲突问题。

文章还提到在终端中运行Emacs的一些缺点，如键位冲突、某些键无法传输、缺乏显示PDF和图像的能力等。同时，终端复用器会干扰Emacs的ANSI控制码处理，导致颜色失配、滚动问题等。

最后，文章介绍了Emacs的客户端-服务器架构，通过`M-x server-start`或`emacs --daemon`可以实现类似终端复用器的功能，从而进一步提升工作流效率。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Emacs作为全自然编辑器与其他专用工具（如终端、tmux等）的对比，讨论它们在功能性和稳定性上的优劣。

不同观点：
• [imiric] 反对将Emacs作为全能工具，认为Emacs的shell和终端模拟器存在问题，如输出损坏、键绑定失效、使用Readline的应用程序异常，以及整体速度较慢。他还提到Emacs的Elisp配置可能会导致终端崩溃或挂起，因此更倾向于使用专门工具（如st、zsh、tmux），并认为不需要让整个工作流依赖单一工具。

• [floren] 指出tmux的一个关键功能——会话共享，即多用户可以同时查看并操作同一会话。这个功能在协作场景中非常有用，而Emacs无法替代这种协作能力。

• [lolive] 以幽默的方式提到过去使用Emacs时遇到的高内存消耗问题，暗示Emacs在资源管理上可能存在不足，呼应了[imiric]对Emacs稳定性的担忧。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于Emacs是否可以作为一个全能工具来替代现代终端和shell组合。imiric明确表示反对，认为Emacs在处理终端任务时存在技术问题且不稳定，而floren则强调了tmux在协作方面的独特优势，进一步质疑了Emacs的全能性。

• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是工作流的依赖性问题。imiric主张使用多个专用工具来实现不同功能，而不是依赖Emacs一个工具，这样可以避免配置问题对整个工作流的影响。

• 对EXWM（Emacs X Window Manager）的批评作为附带意见被提及，表明一些用户对Emacs扩展到其他领域（如窗口管理）持怀疑态度。

43959887.article_content:
If you’re a command line hacker – and I know you are – then I am sure you are familiar with, and possibly use, GNU
screen
or its contemporary replacement,
tmux
. If you are in the process of
switching from Vim to Emacs
, then
tmux
is no doubt a large part of your workflow.
But here’s the thing: you do not need a terminal multiplexer if you are already using Emacs. Emacs can accomplish nearly everything your terminal multiplexer can do. If you’re not a serious user of
screen
or
tmux
, but you’re still addicted to the command line, then I’m sure this article will convince you of the merits of multiplexers, and how Emacs can slot right in. If you’re still unconvinced after having read this article, then my parting advice is to read about the
keyboard shortcuts in GNU readline
as that’ll at least bring more of Emacs to your command line life.
Before I get into the weeds of why, let me just quickly state that, sure,
tmux
and friends will always have their uses: on remote servers for people who insist on running their daemons inside a
screen
session like it’s 1997 (bonus points if it’s an IRC client); and of course for actual terminal use on machines where Emacs is not available, or where you have to work with others who may not know Emacs.
Caveats aside, let me share why I think you should consider using Emacs for some or all of your multiplexing needs, as it can do everything from detaching and re-attaching sessions; to windowing; to terminal emulation and running shells; and even the odd bit of text editing…
The Perils of Terminal Programs
Naturally, terminal multiplexers are meant for terminals, and as such, I’ll talk exclusively about running Emacs in a terminal from now on, although nearly all the advice I write applies equally to GUI Emacs. My thoughts on terminal Emacs are well known if you’re a frequent reader, but I will restate them again by saying that running GUI Emacs is a far better proposition than running Emacs in a terminal (multiplexer or not) for the following simple reasons:
Key Bindings often clash with your terminal
It’s such a common problem for beginners: they fire up Emacs in a terminal, and wonder why some keys don’t work at all. The answer is usually the terminal tool itself. You’ll have to disable their invasive overreach of your key bindings so they pass through to the terminal, but now you lose said key bindings as you may want to use them elsewhere.
Not all key bindings work in a terminal
Despite a lot of bolted-on protocols, additions and extensions made over the years, the fact of the matter is that some keys are simply not possible to represent and transmit to a terminal and the underlying program. This is another common newbie trap.
Lack of fidelity
You cannot view PDFs, use images, or rice your Emacs with fancy SVG icons; some terminal emulators have limited color bit depth. The value of this is debatable, but I find the ability to view PDFs and images useful.
Flow Control Chaos
And the ultimate trap of them all: the ossified flow control feature that some terminals still enable by default. Type
Control+s
in some terminal setups, and your terminal freezes, so as to give you enough time to read the text before it can scroll by.
Control+q
thaws your terminal. A fantastic feature when you’re downloading Dr. Who fan scripts from a dusty newsgroup back in the 1980s. Today… not so much. You can permanently disable flow control with
stty -ixon
, but it’s just one more thing to think about.
There’s one more reason not to run terminal Emacs inside a
terminal multiplexer
and that is… well, everything, actually. The multiplexer gets first dips on the ANSI escape codes terminals use to move the cursor and draw stuff to the screen, and it’s oh-so-easy to break or gum things up. Mismatched colors; loss of color bit-depth; keys not getting translated properly; keys intercepted and repurposed by the multiplexer; weird scrollback and buffering issues; the list goes on and on.
Terminal multiplexers are awesome, but they’re also faced with a tricky problem: they
must
work with nearly everything in a way that is sensible and consistent and often across a wide range of terminal capabilities and platforms. Sure, you can tweak this stuff: do you really want to, though?
So those are the downsides of terminal Emacs with or without the lather of a multiplexer messing with your escape codes. But as annoying as these issues are, terminal Emacs is a full-fledged Emacs experience otherwise.
Now let’s replicate the multiplexing experience inside Emacs.
Emacs’s Client-Server Architecture
Of course Emacs has a client-server architecture. It’s a
text editor!
Run
M-x server-start
in an active Emacs instance and your current Emacs becomes the server host. Note that there are multiple ways of running Emacs in server mode. If you use
emacs --daemon
to start the daemon, you’ll get a persistent daemon that does not spawn a frame; you must then type
emacsclient -c
to connect to your Emacs. A third way is
systemctl --

data.title: Strain gauge made out of PCB
data.author: dr_coffee
data.article_summary: 该项目是一个基于PCB的自制应变计，包含放大器，可测量微米级别的微小形变，全量程为±3厘米。推荐的PCB厚度为0.6毫米，可通过调整厚度改变输出电压。设计包括4元件或2元件的传感桥，并提供加强板以防止弯曲。该应变计可手动组装，兼容Seeed Studio XIAO RP2040微控制器或外部微控制器。外部ADC和偏压生成器可选择性安装。附带的示例固件会在串口打开后进行5秒的偏移校准，并持续采样。可通过脚本绘制自定义传感元件形状并导入KiCad。项目采用MIT许可证。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：DIY毫克精度天平的技术细节和挑战，包括应变片传感器的使用、电压设置以及环境因素的影响。

不同观点：
• knotimpressed 关注的是DIY毫克精度天平的实现，特别是应变片传感器的成本和分辨率是否足够高。
• amelius 提出了关于BRIDGE_SUPPLY电压连接到电压调节器输出和PWM信号的技术问题，通过使用FSA5157L6模拟开关实现。
• rolph 分享了关于压电传感器与应变片传感器的比较资源链接，引导讨论向两种传感器技术的选择和区别。
• fake-name 讨论了自制应变片在温度和湿度变化下的重复性问题，指出环境因素对测量精度的影响，并提出校准的必要性或接受相对值的妥协。

补充讨论：
• fake-name 进一步解释了商用应变片通常使用康斯坦丁电阻元件和聚酰亚胺载体薄膜，以应对温度变化，并且这些元件价格相对低廉。
• amelius 对knotimpressed提到的厚度与输出电压关系提出疑问，认为较薄的板子在相同重量下应产生更大的电压摆幅，这与knotimpressed的预期相反。

争议焦点：主要集中在应变片传感器的环境稳定性及其在DIY项目中的可行性，特别是在温度和湿度变化下的精度和校准问题。

PCB Strain Gauge
A strain gauge, with amplifier, where the sensing element is the circuit board itself. Sensitive enough to measure deflections in the range of micrometers while having a full scale deflection range of +/- 3cm.
strain_demo.mp4
View files with KiCanvas!
Manufacturing
The recommended board thickness is 0.6mm, although it could be made thicker or thinner for different applications. Thinner boards will result in a smaller output voltage swing.
strain_gauge_3.zip
20 mm x 118 mm, 2 layer
0.15mm (~6mil) min trace width
4-element sensing bridge
strain_gauge_3_rotated.zip
Same as the previous one, except it uses 2-element sensing.
Lower thermal drift and bias from manufacturing (theoretically)
stran_gauge_stiffener.zip
20 mm x 42 mm rectangle to keep the component side from flexing
Can be affixed to the board with 3M VHB 5906
Assembly
This project was made with hand-assembly in mind, and does not require hot air or a reflow oven.
The board can be used standalone with an integrated microcontroller (Seeed Studio XIAO RP2040) or an external microcontroller through the header pins.
The external ADC (U5) can be omitted, and the analog voltage can be sampled directly on the "OUT" pin.
The bias voltage generator (U8, U4) can also be omitted by placing a jumper wire between pins 2&3 on U8. Doing this will result in a measureable voltage on the output when no force is applied.
Programming
The included sample firmware will wait until a serial console is opened, perform a 5 second offset calibration, then sample continuously at the lowest gain setting. The
graph.py
script can be used to display the output.
For high sensitivity measurements, it's important to let the board reach a stable operating temperature for at least 5 minutes before calibrating.
Customatization
To customize the shape of the sensing element,
draw_footprint.ipynb
can be used to generate an outline of a given width, height and curvature. The resulting
.svg
can be imported into Inkscape and converted into a KiCad footprint using the
svg2shenzen
tool.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：是否用DANE替代pinning是合理的安全措施

不同观点：
• Phillipseamore认为可以用DANE（DNS-Based Authentication of Named Entities）替代pinning，并认为这种方法仍然有效。此观点表明DANE可以起到与pinning类似的安全作用，可能是因为DANE依赖于DNSSEC（DNS Security Extensions）来确保证书的合法性，从而避免中间人攻击。

补充讨论：
• DANE的支持者可能认为，DANE通过在DNSSEC保护的DNS记录中直接绑定证书信息，提供了另一种方式来验证服务器的身份，从而减少对传统证书颁发机构（CA）的依赖。
• 然而，反对用DANE替代pinning的意见可能会指出，DANE的广泛部署依赖于DNSSEC的普及和正确实施，而目前很多区域的DNSSEC部署并不完善，可能带来额外的风险。
• 争议的焦点可能在于两种技术的安全性、成熟度和部署难度上的差异，特别是在防止中间人攻击和确保通信安全方面的有效性。

总结：评论中主要讨论了是否可以用DANE替代pinning作为确保通信安全的手段，提出了对DANE技术依赖DNSSEC的有效性和部署现状的不同看法。

data.title: Bios Boot to D
data.author: teleforce
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了如何使用D语言编写类似C的语言代码，并使其在PC上通过BIOS引导加载运行。作者对从BIOS启动到现代高级语言的运行过程进行了简要分析，强调了x86 PC的向后兼容性。文章首先介绍了汇编语言的基础知识，解释了汇编指令与硬件寄存器的关系，以及如何用标签模拟高级语言中的变量。接着，文章描述了启动过程：BIOS进行硬件自检，然后从磁盘加载前512字节，检查是否为可引导扇区（以0x55和0xAA为标记），并将这512字节加载到内存地址0x7c00开始执行。作者计划将D语言代码直接放在引导扇区后的磁盘空间中，并在16位实模式下运行。虽然实模式与早期x86设备兼容，但其功能有限，许多现代x86特性无法使用。

43958968.article_content:
After my previous post on
using D for C-like programming
, I
wondered about going deeper. Whatâs the minimum it would take to run C-like D code on a PC? Could it run straight from
a BIOS bootloader?
If you seriously want to make an OS, youâre much better off using an existing bootloader like U-Boot or GRUB, or at
least using UEFI. But doing it this way is interesting because the x86 PC has an insane level of backwards
compatibility, and booting from the BIOS to a modern high-level language is like doing an archealogical dig through the
past 40 years of computing history.
Super Quick Crash Course in Assembly Language
Assembly language is just a more readable machine code. Every assembly instruction translates to a binary machine
code instruction, and vice versa. I use Intel syntax (specifically NASM syntax), which would probably be a de facto
standard if GNU toolchains (
gcc
, and so on) didnât use
AT&T syntax for
hysterical
historical reasons. I first learned this stuff hacking around on MS-DOS, and
I still prefer Intel syntax.
This code:
mov
ax
,
0x20
is like
ax
=
32
;
except that
ax
isnât a normal variable in memory, itâs a
hardware
register
in the CPU, but it holds integer values in much the same way.
0x20
is just the number
32
written in the hexadecimal number system, rather than the usual
decimal system. Either system can be used, but hexadecimal just happens to be more natural when working with low-level
stuff. There are plently of tutorials explaining how to convert the two, and you possibly already have some kind of
calculator on your computer that can do conversion for you.
Normal variables are just numbered addresses in memory. You put a value into some addressed location, and itâs up to
you to remember where you put it. Actually, the
NASM assembler
lets us give labels to
the addresses, mimicking variables in a high-level language, but it all turns into raw addresses in machine code. If
you disassemble machine code back into assembly, you lose any labels.
mov
byte
[
0x8000
],
42
; Store a value in memory
mov
byte
[
the_magic_number
],
42
; Same thing, but we've defined a meaningful label for the address
There are no control structures like
if
statements and
while
loops, only
goto
statements (or âjumpsâ in x86 assembly). For example, this code
byte
foo
=
6
;
// stuff
if
(
foo
==
6
)
{
// do something
}
would be implemented as something like
db
foo
6
; stuff
cmp
byte
[
foo
],
6
; Compare with 6
jne
skip_do_something
; Jump (if) Not Equal
; do something
skip_do_something:
Once again, in machine code, jumps actually go to raw memory addresses, but the assembler lets us give them
meaningful labels. The
cmp
instruction sets bits in a special
register called the
flags
register, and thatâs how the
jne
instruction detects the result.
Thatâs enough assembly to follow this post, but if you want a deeper understanding, there are
good tutorials
around. One more thing that
I should mention is that even if something might seem like syntactically good assembly, it might not actually be an
operation supported by the hardware. So often a little extra juggling around is needed to get things done.
The Journey Begins
When you first power on a PC, the Basic Input/Output System (BIOS) is the first thing that starts. At least, Iâll
pretend it is because modern systems are still compatible with that. The BIOS first does a Power On Self Test (POST) of
the basic hardware. Older BIOSes used to make a cheerful chirp through the PC speaker when this passed, but that seems
to have gone out of fashion.
(Update: Itâs more like
PC speakers have gone out of
fashion
. Thanks agent-plaid)
Next the BIOS goes through each disk in some order, loading the first 512 bytes
and checking if the last two bytes are
0x55
and
0xaa
. Thatâs the marker for a bootable disk. Why 512 bytes? Because, for
performance reasons, disks work in 512-byte chunks called sectors, instead of operating byte-by-byte. Why
0x55
and
0xaa
?
I donât know; thatâs just the way it is.
(Update: crimaniak explains that itâs to
avoid booting from a bad
drive
.)
Anyway, the raw 512 bytes from the bootable disk are copied verbatim to address
0x7c00
, and then the BIOS starts the CPU executing from there. This is
where our job begins.
This bootloader is simpler than ones like GRUB, so all the boot code will be in the first 512 bytes of the disk
image, and the OS payload (the D code) will sit directly after it.
First Steps
Letâs trace through the code.
We land at
0x7c00
with the x86 chip running in whatâs
called
16b real mode
. This is backwards compatible with very early x86 devices, and is designed for old
computer systems that run one program at a time, with full access to the entire machine. This might sound ideal for
what weâre doing, but Intel engineers realised that âreal modeâ wasnât the future of computing around the time of the
286 (1982), and many x86 features since then are not supported in real mode. The most obvious limit

data.title: Fandom sells gaming media brand Giant Bomb to long-term staff
data.author: minimaxir
data.article_summary: 2025年5月10日，粉丝平台Fandom将游戏媒体品牌Giant Bomb出售给其长期员工及内容创作者Jeff Bakalar和Jeff Grubb。交易细节未公开，Giant Bomb的节目将在交易完成后尽快恢复。Fandom表示，此举旨在让Giant Bomb回归独立根源，相信Jeff和Jeff能延续其 legacy。Jeff Bakalar和Jeff Grubb感谢粉丝支持，并表示未来将由社区支持团队运营，更多计划将陆续公布。Giant Bomb以独特风格提供游戏新闻、评论和视频内容，自2008年成立以来在业界具有影响力。

43950046.article_content:
Fandom Sells Giant Bomb to Independent Creators
May 10, 2025
Gaming Content Creators & Long-Time Giant Bomb Staff Jeff Bakalar & Jeff Grubb Taking Full Ownership & Operations of the Gaming Media Brand
News Announced on Stage During Giant Bomb Panel at PAX East Conference
San Francisco, CA - May 10, 2025
-
Fandom
, the world’s largest fan platform, is selling
Giant Bomb
to long-time Giant Bomb staff and gaming content creators Jeff Bakalar and Jeff Grubb. Financials of the deal were not disclosed. Giant Bomb’s programming, which was paused in order to work out the terms of this deal, will resume as quickly as possible. More details will be communicated soon by Giant Bomb’s new owners.
Statement from Fandom
“Fandom has made the strategic decision to transition Giant Bomb back to its independent roots and the brand has been acquired by longtime staff and content creators, Jeff Bakalar and Jeff Grubb, who will now own and operate the site independently. Fans are at the core of everything we do at Fandom and we’re committed to not only serving them but also supporting the creators they love, and the sale of Giant Bomb represents a natural extension of that mission. We’re confident Giant Bomb is in good hands and its legacy will live on with Jeff and Jeff.”
Joint Statement from Jeff Bakalar and Jeff Grubb
"Giant Bomb is now owned by the people who make Giant Bomb, and it would not have been possible without the speedy efforts of Fandom and our mutual agreement on what’s best for fans and creators. The future of Giant Bomb is now in the hands of our supporting community, who have always had our backs no matter what. We'll have a lot more to say about what this looks like soon, but for now, everyone can trust that all the support we receive goes directly to this team."
About Fandom
Fandom is the world’s largest fan platform where fans immerse themselves in imagined worlds across entertainment and gaming. Fandom’s Gaming division manages the online video game retailer Fanatical. Fandom Media, the content arm of Fandom, enhances the fan experience through curated editorial, video and branded content from trusted and established media brands Gamespot, TV Guide, Metacritic and the Emmy-nominated Honest Trailers from Screen Junkies. For more information follow @getfandom or visit:

About Giant Bomb
Giant Bomb is a video game media brand and personality-driven network of gaming-focused content creators that features gaming news, reviews, commentary, and video. Founded in 2008, it offers unmatched access to the games industry with a focus on authenticity, while also covering the business in a unique and irreverent style. Giant Bomb pioneered many of the game content templates of today before they were internet mainstays and provides unique perspectives from a diverse range of industry personalities spanning multiple generations and decades of experience.
